history.title: A Brief History of the Python Programming Language
history.period1.title: 1980s: The Idea and Early Development
history.period1.text: Python was conceived in the late 1980s by Guido van Rossum as a successor to the ABC language, designed to handle exceptions and interface with the Amoeba operating system.
history.period2.title: 1991: Birth of Python 0.9.0
history.period2.text: Guido released the first version of the code — Python 0.9.0. It already featured classes with inheritance, exception handling, functions, and core data types: lists, dictionaries, and strings.
history.period3.title: 2000: Python 2.0
history.period3.text: Python 2.0 introduced major features such as garbage collection and Unicode support. This dramatically increased its popularity, especially in academia and startups.
history.period4.title: 2008: Python 3.0 (Python 3000)
history.period4.text: Python 3.0 was released as a major, mostly backward-incompatible overhaul. It cleaned up many longstanding design flaws, though the transition took years. The most visible change: print became a function — print().
history.period5.title: 2020: End of Life for Python 2
history.period5.text: Official support for Python 2.7 ended permanently, marking the final push for the entire ecosystem to migrate to Python 3 — now the only officially supported version.
history.conclusion.title: Impact and Future
history.conclusion.text: Python continues to evolve under community governance. Today it dominates machine learning (TensorFlow, PyTorch), data science (Pandas, NumPy), web development (Django, Flask), automation, and remains one of the most loved and widely used programming languages worldwide.
docs.title: Official Python Documentation (Learning Edition)
docs.section1.title: 1. Introduction: What is Python?
docs.section1.p1: Python is an interpreted, high-level, general-purpose programming language created by Guido van Rossum and first released in 1991.
docs.section1.p2: Its design philosophy emphasizes code readability through the use of significant whitespace (indentation).
docs.section2.title: 2. Installation and Setup
docs.section2.p1: Always use the latest stable version of Python 3. Download the installer from the official site: python.org.
docs.section2.p2: On Windows, make sure to check "Add Python to PATH" during installation.
docs.section3.title: 3. Basic Syntax
docs.section3.p1: Unlike most languages, Python uses colons (:) and indentation (typically 4 spaces) to define code blocks.
docs.section4.title: 4. Data Types and Structures
docs.section4.p1: Python includes powerful built-in data structures: lists, dictionaries, tuples, and sets.
docs.section5.title: 5. Functions and Modules
docs.section5.p1: Functions are defined with the def keyword and can accept arguments, return values, and include type hints.
docs.section6.title: 6. Object-Oriented Programming (OOP)
docs.section6.p1: Python offers full support for OOP paradigms: inheritance, polymorphism, encapsulation, and abstraction.
docs.section7.title: 7. Working with Files
docs.section7.p1: Use the open() function for file operations. The with statement ensures files are properly closed, even if an error occurs.
docs.section8.title: 8. Exception Handling
docs.section8.p1: Runtime errors are managed using try, except, else, and finally blocks.
docs.section9.title: 9. The Python Standard Library (Stdlib)
docs.section9.p1: The standard library is a rich collection of modules available out-of-the-box. Key modules include os, sys, json, datetime, and re (regular expressions).
docs.section10.title: 10. Virtual Environments
docs.section10.p1: A virtual environment (venv) isolates project dependencies, preventing version conflicts across projects.
docs.section10.p2: Create with: python -m venv my_env. Activate on Windows:

faq.cat1.title: Python Basics
faq.cat1.q1: What is Python and what is it used for?
faq.cat1.a1.p1: Python is a high-level, interpreted, general-purpose programming language known for its clean and readable syntax — making it ideal for beginners.
faq.cat1.a1.li2: Data Science & Machine Learning (Pandas, NumPy, TensorFlow)
faq.cat1.q2: Which Python version should I use?
faq.cat1.a2.p1: Always use the latest stable Python 3 release (currently 3.11+).
faq.cat1.a2.p2: Python 2 reached end-of-life in 2020 and is no longer supported.
faq.cat1.q3: Why does Python use indentation instead of braces?
faq.cat1.a3.p1: Python enforces indentation (usually 4 spaces) to delimit code blocks — a feature known as "significant whitespace".
faq.cat1.a3.p2: Guido van Rossum chose this to force clean, consistent formatting and greatly improve code readability.

lec14.intro.title: 1. Introduction: What is inheritance?
lec14.intro.def: Inheritance – in object-oriented programming (OOP), it is the mechanism of creating a new class based on an existing one. The existing class is the base (parent) class. The new class is the derived (child) class.

lec14.idea.item2: Other classes inherit them and, if needed, extend or override them.
